subject: fang blenny
title: A 2-Inch Fish Has Fangs, and a Painless Bite Laced With Opioids

scenes.text: This tiny fish has fangs, and its bite doesn't hurt. That's the scary part.
Fang blennies are about two inches long, with two huge fangs in the lower jaw.
In 2017, scientists let them bite cotton swabs and took the venom apart.
Injected into mice, it caused no signs of pain at all.
Instead it carries an opioid-like peptide, and in rats it made blood pressure drop sharply.
So a bigger fish that grabs one may suddenly go weak and let go. Painless doesn't mean harmless.

description:
Fang blennies (Meiacanthus) are about 2 inches long with two large fangs in the lower jaw, and they are the only fish known to deliver venom with a bite.
A 2017 Current Biology study found the venom contains an opioid peptide, a neuropeptide also found in cone snails and a lipase like one in scorpion venom. It caused no pain in mice but a sharp drop in blood pressure in rats, which may slow down a predator long enough for the blenny to escape.
Which small animal would you least want to bite you?
first_comment: Its fangs evolved before its venom, the reverse of snakes. Which tiny animal surprised you the most?
